newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone-Poulenc shares jump after results.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc shares jump after results.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc shares jumped more than two percent in opening trade on the Paris stock exchange after the group announced third quarter results including a rise in net income to 756 million francs from 669 million previously.
The share hit a year high of 145.9 francs, up more than two percent from Thursday's closing price, in the opening exchanges and stood 1.47 percent higher at 144.6 francs at 0811 GMT.
Rhone said net sales had risen to 20.468 billion francs from 19.621 billion and operating profit to 2.054 billion verus 1.828 billion for the same quarter a year earlier.
It announced a charge of 81 million francs for withdrawal of its Albumin products produced in a venture between Hoechst and U.S. unit Rhone-Poulenc Rorer.
Rhone-Poulenc finance director Jean-Pierre Tirouflet told a news conference the company would take a total charge, including this sum, of between 100 and 200 million francs at the net level in 1996.
Regarding the outlook, when questioned about a forecast of 2.5 billion francs for full-year net profit, Tirouflet said: "I have lower forecasts in my head".
